# MACD with HTF Panels [theUltimator5]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

MACD with HTF Panels combines a conventional chart-timeframe MACD with small independent higher-timeframe views drawn to its side. It aims to keep momentum context visible without chart switching and demonstrates a reusable presentation method for other indicators. Each panel has its own timeframe calculation while sharing common indicator settings. The table remains broader than the visible panel count, so hiding a panel does not imply its numerical values disappear.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for ordinary chart-only EMA MACD line/signal/histogram with chosen lengths/source. HTF mapping/confirmation, panel scaling and exact publication averaging defaults remain caveats.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Narrow chart-only ordinary MACD: declare source X and lengths F,S,G; MACD=EMA_F(X)−EMA_S(X), Signal=EMA_G(MACD), Histogram=MACD−Signal. This declares the ordinary EMA convention for the source-named standard MACD rather than claiming undocumented default lengths or selectable-average parity. Disable HTF panels.
- Calculate MACD line, signal and histogram with adjustable lengths and color the histogram by both sign and slope.
- Draw higher-timeframe mini-charts with optional candles; position horizontally in bars and scale candle heights using ATR.

## Outputs and intended use

- Compare momentum direction and change across the current chart and higher timeframes.
- A table shows all four higher-timeframe MACD, signal and histogram values regardless of how many panels are visible.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Up to five total timeframes are supported: current plus four higher-timeframe panels.
- Four panels default to a 2x2 layout; one to three stack vertically. Candles default off and table defaults bottom right.
- Caller supplies source and fast/slow/signal lengths under the stated EMA convention. Show HTF panels off selects the chart-only fallback; numeric MACD defaults are not given.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Unconfirmed higher-timeframe values may evolve; displayed agreement is not an entry rule.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- MACD averaging types/default lengths, automatic timeframe mapping, ATR scale formula and higher-timeframe confirmation policy are absent.

# Machine Learning Pivot Points (KNN) [SS]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

## Idea and objective

Compare the current regression slope with slope signatures collected before confirmed turning points to flag possible approaching pivots.

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** The feature concept and default signature lengths are disclosed, but the classifier output and confidence cannot be reproduced from the prose.

- Exact slope/distance normalization
- Cluster confidence and signal rule
- Training memory and outcome-label rules

## How it works

- At each confirmed high/low pivot, store the regression slope of its preceding signature window. Compare current rolling slope with historical high/low classes using nearest-neighbor distances and derive a relative cluster-similarity confidence.

## Outputs and intended use

- A live table shows high/low bias and similarity; a separate proof-of-concept table reports reversal occurrence and subsequent moves. Glowing markers give way to ordinary triangles when polyline limits constrain history.

## Parameters and stated settings

- K defaults two. The described training uses ten-bar pivots and twenty-bar slope signatures, with pivot left/right and signature-window settings adjustable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- A ninety-percent similarity description is not a calibrated ninety-percent reversal probability. Pivot labels become known only after confirmation, and training/test separation is not demonstrated.

- Slope normalization, exact distance aggregation, confidence mapping, success/reversal definition, training-window limits and signal gating are absent.

# Liquidity Void Detector (Zeiierman)

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Liquidity Void Detector emphasizes unusually large recent returns when volume is weak relative to its own baseline. It explicitly offers a practical OHLCV proxy, not measured order-book emptiness. The narrative associates upward low-volume moves with potential downside refill and downward moves with upside refill, but its settings section reverses those buy/sell labels, so consumers must preserve that contradiction rather than wire labels into orders.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Parameterized numerical void oscillator is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Compute log volume relative to its SMA and Z-score that shock; compute and Z-score one-bar log return.
- Multiply return Z-score by full weight in low-volume conditions or by a configurable fade otherwise.
- volTrend=SMA(volume,L);vs=log(volume)-log(volTrend) for positive inputs;vsZ=ZScore(vs,vzLen);lowVS=(vsZ<=vzThr). r1=log(close/close[1]);retZ=ZScore(r1,rLen);osc=retZ*(1 if lowVS else fadeNoLow). ZScore=(x-mean)/std under caller convention with nonzero std;fadeNoLow in[0,1]. Contradictory side labels and signal decisions remain excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Inspect signed low-participation displacement alongside price zones and other tools; do not assume voids necessarily fill.
- Usable scope: Parameterized numerical void oscillator. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Low-volume threshold examples are -0.5 to -1.0. Fade ranges 0–1, with zero ignoring non-low-volume bars and one ignoring the volume condition. Lengths/oscillator thresholds are configurable without defaults.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: weak reported volume is not actual depth, standardized returns can be unstable and the narrative/settings side labels contradict.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Exact zScore convention, zero-variance/invalid-volume behavior, default lookbacks and unambiguous trigger-label mapping are missing.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: ohlcv.

The author explicitly doubts signal accuracy and observes that signals often occur in low-volume/low-volatility conditions. ## How it works

- Unsmoothed raw-envelope scope: q_t=Volume_t/(Volume_t+Volume_(t−1)), using the current and preceding candle volume. A zero denominator requires an explicit caller policy; none is supplied.

- Optionally smooth volume; average derived bounds to form bands and classify high/low crosses by candle direction.

# Hurst Exponent

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Estimate persistence or mean-reverting tendency in a market series using rescaled-range analysis across several sample sizes.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

**Partly disclosed computation.** A core specification remains unresolved: Input transformation, partition overlap, standard-deviation convention, regression weighting and degenerate-sample handling are unspecified.

- Input transformation, partition overlap, standard-deviation convention, regression weighting and degenerate-sample handling are unspecified.

## How it works

- Divide a chosen lookback into shorter samples, calculate rescaled range at each sample size and fit a power law by regressing log rescaled range against log sample size. The slope is the Hurst estimate.

## Outputs and intended use

- Interpret estimates above one-half as persistence and below one-half as a mean-reversion tendency, following the author's heuristic. Use it as regime context rather than a directional signal.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Select lookback and up to eight sample sizes; zero disables a sample. A start-date input limits computation when platform runtime limits are hit.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Finite samples, trends and changing volatility can bias R/S estimates. The interpretation is statistical tendency, not a guarantee that the next move follows a particular regime.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Input transformation, partition overlap, standard-deviation convention, regression weighting and degenerate-sample handling are unspecified.

## Idea and objective

This projection study extrapolates a smoothed input using its latest slope and average second difference, then draws a family of curves with different acceleration dampening factors. It also serves as an educational example of nested arrays and user-defined types. The curves are deterministic what-if paths for a moving-average-like series, not probability bands or independently validated forecasts.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Explicit slope, acceleration and quadratic dampened projection expressions define the principal scenario paths with caller-selected lengths/factors.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Calculate a simple moving average baseline, first difference for slope and average second difference over an acceleration window.
- Create several quadratic paths from initial value, slope and dampened acceleration, storing each path’s points/color/factor in a structured array.
- Optionally delete prior polylines before drawing new projections; an offset can anchor an earlier observation.

## Outputs and intended use

- Compare the fan of differently curved scenarios and optionally retain old projections for inspection.

## Parameters and stated settings

- The code initializes nine curves. Inputs include SMA length, acceleration window, source, offset, initial/growth dampening, prediction length and history cleanup; no numeric defaults are listed.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: quadratic acceleration extrapolation can diverge quickly and the family has no calibrated probability interpretation. Prose calls SMA smoothed and simple inconsistently.

## How it works

- Cascade a two-pole high-pass filter with a two-pole SuperSmoother low-pass filter, then divide the result by RMS. High-pass critical period limits longest waves and low-pass period limits shortest waves.

## Outputs and intended use

- Trend display colors by zero sign; Threshold display uses a gray line and highlights user-defined extremes. This is a filtered market representation, not direct evidence of stable future cycles.

- Default passband spans twenty-to-thirty bars; an example longer high-pass setting is 250. RMS length is configurable, minimum low-pass above eight is recommended and high-pass must not be below low-pass.

## Failure modes and caveats

- RMS-scaled amplitudes are standard-deviation-like only under suitable distribution/mean assumptions. Filter choices alter phase/lag, and invalid bandwidth produces a runtime error.

# Trading Activity Index (Zeiierman)

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Trading Activity Index measures whether smoothed price-times-volume is unusual relative to its own recent history. It highlights participation regimes using a log transform, percentile guides and color normalization. The author connects activity with breakout conviction, but the computation measures reported bar activity rather than liquidity depth, trade size distribution or institutional identities.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Log dollar-volume and percentile references is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Multiply close by volume, smooth with a configurable SMA and log-transform the result.
- Calculate rolling interpolated percentiles and a normalized rank for gradient coloring.
- D=close*volume;A=SMA(D,len_form);vscale=log(A) for A>0. Over caller len_hist compute linearly interpolated20th,40th,60th,80th percentiles. Color rank normalization,feed-volume units and nonpositive-domain behavior remain limitations.

## Outputs and intended use

- Read blue as quieter activity and orange/red as stronger activity; compare activity percentile with price setups instead of treating it as directional prediction.
- Usable scope: Log dollar-volume and percentile references. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Guides use 20/40/60/80 percentiles and color rank spans 0–1. Formation/history windows are configurable without defaults.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: multiplying volume already reported in quote currency can double-convert units, and log transformation needs positive values. High volume does not prove liquidity or follow-through.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Exact 0–1 rank-normalization equation, zero-volume handling, volume units and default windows are not supplied.

## Idea and objective

Volume-based Support & Resistance Zones marks high-volume swing extremes across several timeframes. A zone extends from the fractal extreme to its candle close, combining a turning-point reference with the size of the rejection region. The author says larger zones are more significant, but that is a qualitative interpretation rather than a tested ranking. The indicator offers extensive history, drawing and alert controls without supplying a complete trading setup.

## How it works

- Require fractal highs with three successive higher highs followed by two lower highs, with inverse logic for lows.
- Gate fractals by volume above its configurable moving average.
- Draw extreme-to-close zones per timeframe, retain bounded history and suppress lower-timeframe zones on higher charts.

## Outputs and intended use

- Up to four timeframe zone sets, lines/labels/extensions and configurable alerts support level monitoring.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Four timeframes; per-timeframe volume-average value, zone count and alert types plus styling/visibility are configurable.
- Fractal sequence uses three rising and two falling highs; defaults for MA/timeframes are absent.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Fractals confirm after the turning point; historical zone origins can appear earlier than availability.
- Older higher-timeframe origins may fall back to a bounded history position, especially on stocks.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Volume MA type/length defaults, exact volume comparison timing, equal-extreme treatment, invalidation and alert predicates are absent.

## Idea and objective

Elastic Volume-Weighted Student-T Tension builds adaptive location/dispersion bands and a relative-position oscillator. It aims to account for heavy tails and changing participation rather than assume fixed normal volatility. Volume influences the elastic mean and variance; true range substitutes when volume is unavailable. A higher-timeframe normalization option changes the weighting scale. - Normalize price within the band structure into a percent-B-like oscillator.

- Example HTF choices include 200-day, weekly and monthly.

- Estimated tail parameters can be unstable and distributional fitting does not guarantee mean reversion.
- Volume fallback changes the weighting meaning across symbols.

# Session Edge Profiler | Flux Charts

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Session Edge Profiler measures completed-session behavior and compares the developing session with its own weekday-filtered history. It aims to replace generic claims about Asia, London or New York with instrument-specific evidence. The dashboard covers range, volume, directional persistence, daily extremes and explicitly defined structural counts. Its alert identifies unusually large range rather than a directional trade. The source provides enough parameterized lifecycle and metric rules to reproduce a substantive session-statistics specification, while realistic execution and future profitability remain outside its purpose.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** The source defines the financial computation and parameterized inputs sufficiently for a reproducible specification.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Track each enabled session’s OHLCV/events in New York time, commit completed records at the shifted trading-day boundary and filter history by selected weekday.
- Normalize session range by previous completed daily ATR; average normalized ranges and count historical values at/below the current normalized range for percentile.
- Bull means session close > session open. Continuation means its bullish/bearish direction matches the previous occurrence of that same session; exclude the first occurrence from the eligible denominator. Bull%=100×bull count/all sessions; Continuation%=100×matched count/eligible sessions. Volume share is session volume divided by summed completed enabled-session volume; daily-extreme flags compare session extremes with full trading-day extremes.
- At active-session bar t, bullish FVG is Low_t>High_(t−2), storing High_(t−2); bearish FVG is High_t<Low_(t−2), storing Low_(t−2). Later within the same session, invalidate/remove a bullish gap if close falls below its stored level or a bearish gap if close rises above its stored level. Survival%=100×(formed−invalidated)/formed at session end; later-session invalidation does not change that result.
- Confirm pivots with the chosen number of bars on each side. A subsequent close above a confirmed high or below a confirmed low increments the active-session swing-break counter and consumes that pivot so it cannot be counted again. A newly confirmed high above the previous tracked session high pivot increments HH; a newly confirmed low below the previous tracked session low pivot increments LL.

## Outputs and intended use

- Thirteen dashboard metrics, session boxes, live range/average/percentile label and high-percentile alert support session research.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Five default NY windows: Asia 19–02, London 02–08:30, NY AM 08:30–12, Lunch 12–13:30, PM 13:30–16. Day boundary 18:00 NY via six-hour shift.
- ATR length default 14, range 5–50; pivot strength default five each side, range 2–20. Weekdays default on, weekends off.
- Range alert exceeds 90th percentile. Tier cutoffs are 75/25 for percentile and 70/40 for FVG survival.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Live partial-session range is compared with complete historical sessions, so percentile is not time-of-session adjusted.
- Volume denominator is summed enabled completed sessions, not necessarily all market-day volume; overlaps can double-count.
- FVG survival means survival only until that session ends.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Tie/zero-denominator and interrupted-session edge cases need implementation choices; no trade-execution model is intended.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: intraday ohlcv, daily ATR history, New York timezone/session calendar.

Repository input-class support: unavailable or unresolved. The specification is substantive, but usable aligned intraday history/session coverage has not been established.

# Realtime 5D Profile [LucF]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Realtime 5D Profile accumulates live chart updates into price-level distributions of volume or update counts. It encodes level activity, directional imbalance and age, offering an evolving view of where observed participation occurred. Unlike a historical profile, it starts when loaded and loses its accumulated state when refreshed or re-executed. The source carefully distinguishes chart updates from exchange transactions, so its tick label must not be interpreted as a complete trade tape on aggregated charts.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for up/down update-count totals/delta on supplied ordered updates with explicit first-update convention and timeframe reset. Volume extraction, level rebinning, age rendering and trend-reset parity remain incomplete.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Independent aggregate activity counts: for ordered chart updates, compare price with the previous update; increment UpCount on higher price, DownCount on lower price, and carry the last known direction when unchanged. Totals are UpCount+DownCount and delta UpCount−DownCount. Use a selected timeframe reset; seed from the first observed price and begin counting once a comparison/known polarity exists. This explicit first-update exclusion is a caller convention because source initialization is not stated.
- Assign each update to up/down using price versus the preceding update, retaining the last direction when unchanged.
- Bin updates around dynamic price levels; rebalance historical updates when the profile range changes. Line lengths scale to the largest level and age comes from average update times.
- Render double-sided down/up profiles or single-sided totals/deltas; reset by selected timeframes or trend changes.

## Outputs and intended use

- Compare participation and recency with line width, thickness, totals, tooltips and Data Window values.
- No alerts are included; the author suggests small-timeframe use with infrequent chart changes.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Four line thicknesses encode age. An example 20-level double profile needs 42 labels against a 500-label limit.
- The author reports handling upwards of 60K updates per profile, not a guaranteed capacity.
- Choose tick/update-count mode and a timeframe reset (chart timeframe resets each new bar). Caller first-update policy is explicitly excluded until direction is known; this is not claimed as default-code parity.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Live-only state cannot be reconstructed from historical OHLCV.
- Uptick/downtick classification can misclassify true aggressor flow; prolonged accumulation may exhaust memory.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Precise rebinning boundaries, age-to-thickness thresholds and trend-reset implementations are not fully disclosed.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: live timestamped price and volume chart updates.

# Trend Target Ribbon [BOSWaves]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Trend Target Ribbon combines ALMA trend confirmation with a chart-based position plan. A directional flip creates an entry reference, structural risk distance and staged reward levels, while a gradient ribbon conveys the strength of the existing trend.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for configured trend-state flips and ATR-clamped structural risk with caller calculation settings/initial state; ribbon conviction, target spacing and intrabar event ordering remain outside scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Configured trend rule: B=ALMA(source,length,offset,sigma), slope=(B-B[k])/ATR and band width=confirmation*SD(source,deviation length). Flip bullish only if slope>minimum and close>B+width, bearish only if slope<-minimum and close<B-width, and only on a changed state. At a flip entry E=close; long raw risk=E-lowestLow(stop lookback), short raw risk=highestHigh(stop lookback)-E. Clamp risk to [minimumATR*ATR,maximumATR*ATR] and place stop E-risk for long or E+risk for short. Caller supplies all selected calculation settings and initial state.
- The baseline is an ALMA of the selected source. Its change over a configurable slope lookback is divided by ATR. Bullish confirmation requires positive slope above its threshold and a close above the ALMA plus a standard-deviation confirmation band; bearish confirmation reverses both conditions. State changes only when the qualifying direction differs from the current state.
- On a flip, entry is the closing price. The recent swing low for longs or high for shorts supplies raw risk, clamped between minimum and maximum ATR distances. Successive equidistant R targets extend in the trade direction. Bar extremes track stops and target hits; an opposing flip freezes the previous drawing.
- Conviction blends doubled slope magnitude and price separation from ALMA to control a layered ribbon and candle brightness. Old position drawings are removed when the history limit is exceeded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Directional diamonds and alerts identify flips. Entry, stop, risk zone, target lines and persistent checkmarks support visual planning and staged discretionary exits. Proximity glow highlights approaching targets; faded plans preserve recent signal history.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Suggested baseline: ALMA length 34, confirmation 0.65, slope minimum 0.08, structural lookback 12, stop ATR bounds 0.75 and 3.0, four targets and four visible positions. Source, ALMA offset/sigma, slope/deviation lookbacks, projection length and approach radius are configurable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Choppy markets can produce rapid opposing plans. ATR clamping can move a stop away from actual structure. Drawn target touches do not establish executable fills, intrabar event order or measured returns.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- ATR and deviation lengths, ALMA offset/sigma defaults, exact conviction normalization and R-spacing coefficient are not supplied. Simultaneous stop/target handling is not defined.

Required inputs: ohlcv.

# real_time_candles

**Classification:** financial-library. Native publication type: library. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

real_time_candles builds candle objects from live samples of prices or other financial series. It supports chart-synchronized candles and independently sampled time/count candles, exposing both their OHLC state and drawing helpers. Its financial uses include watching an oscillator change within a bar or examining short-lived price structures. This is not merely a graphics utility: its central output is sampled financial-series candles, although the claimed trading edge is not validated by the description.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Usable for synchronized ordinary sampled-source OHLC under the documented current/history state and carried-close reset. Custom-time units/overshoot, Heikin-Ashi and EMA implementations remain outside scope.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Narrow chart-synchronized ordinary sampled-source OHLC: select candlestick style and wait_for_sync; begin at a new chart bar. Within a bar retain current source as Close, maximum/minimum of included source samples as High/Low and starting sample as Open. At subsequent chart boundaries the shown reset carries prior sampled Close into Open, seeds the new sample buffer with that Open and appends new observations; thus the carry is included in High/Low. Current object is index0 and completed objects are inserted at index1.
- Capture source values, elapsed milliseconds and sequential update indices with persistent intrabar state.
- Update the current candle at array index zero and preserve completed candles at later indices. Custom candles close when accumulated update count or elapsed time reaches the configured threshold.
- Expose candle arrays, single objects or tuples, standard/Heikin-Ashi styles, extracted components and EMA/drawing methods.

## Outputs and intended use

- Use candles as inputs for custom indicators or render them with time/bar-index coordinates and optional moving averages.
- The example labelled fast RSI actually extracts candle closes; it does not itself calculate a custom-timeframe RSI.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Examples include RSI length 14, 20-second candles with EMA 9 and 15-update candles. Recommended history is 5000 bars and drawing limits 500 each.
- Timezone display offsets span -12 to +12; tied_open connects a new open to the preceding close.
- Choose source (default close), ordinary CandleType.candlestick and synchronization to a new bar. For exact parity preserve the shown carried-close reset; starting/reconnection behavior outside synchronized complete bars is not specified.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Historical bars cannot recover missing live updates, so custom candles cannot be historically backtested from this source.
- An execution update is not necessarily a single exchange trade.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Full boundary overshoot/gap behavior, Heikin-Ashi recurrence and sampling-time units need clarification; the shown time threshold compares seconds against a duration documented in milliseconds.
